title: FEC MUR 8350: Culp for Congress
text:
### Complaint, Responses, Designation of Counsel and Extensions of Time
MUR835000009
RECEIVED
By CELA at 7:57 am, Feb 03, 2025
Federal Election Commission
Office of Complaints Examination & Legal Administration
Attn: Trace Keys, Paralegal
1050 First Street, NE
Washington, DC 20463
Re: MUR 8350
In response to the complaint filed against Culp for Congress, the Committee responds as follows.
The Committee did not omit debt from its reports and was unaware of the claimed debt. Upon the
conclusion of the campaign, in 2022, the Committee paid what they believed to be the total owed to the
vendor, Dave's Campaign Business Solutions.
The four invoices being claimed by the vendor as unpaid, were thought to have been paid by the
Committee and being sent as a clerical error on the part of the vendor. The Committee does not have
record of the vendor reaching out to the treasurer to inquire about payment. The automated emails
sent to the Committee from Quickbooks for the four invoices were discontinued and the Committee
assumed the clerical error was corrected.
Further, per the invoices which were attached to the original complaint, the pricing offered on the
invoices was for invoices paid in full at the time of order, further leading the committee to believe that if
the service had been offered, then the invoices had been paid.
There is no written agreement between the vendor and Campaign to provide services and the
Committee has been terminated since December of 2022.
The Committee was committed to accurate reporting throughout the length of the campaign.
Thank you,
Elizabeth Curtis

### Complaint, Responses, Designation of Counsel and Extensions of Time
MUR835000007
FEDERAL ELECTION COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, DC
November 21, 2024
VIA EMAIL
liz@lizcurtisassociates.com
Elizabeth Curtis, Treasurer
Culp for Congress
P.O. Box 726
Moses Lake, WA 98837
RE: MUR 8350
Dear Ms. Curtis:
The Federal Election Commission (FEC) received a complaint that indicates
Culp for Congress and you in your official capacity as treasurer may have violated the Federal
Election Campaign Act of 1971, as amended (the “Act”). A copy of the complaint is enclosed.
We have numbered this matter MUR 8350. Please refer to this number in all future
correspondence.
The Act affords you the opportunity to demonstrate in writing that no action should be
taken against Culp for Congress and you in your official capacity as treasurer in this matter. If
you wish to file a response, you may submit any factual or legal materials that you believe are
relevant to the Commission’s consideration of this matter. Where appropriate, statements should
be submitted under oath by persons with relevant knowledge. Your response, which should be
addressed to the General Counsel’s Office, must be submitted within 15 days of receipt of this
letter. If no response is received within 15 days, the Commission may take further action based
on the available information.
This matter will remain confidential in accordance with 52 U.S.C. § 30109(a)(4)(B) and
§ 30109(a)(12)(A) unless you notify the Commission in writing that you wish the matter to be
made public. Please be advised that, although the Commission cannot disclose information
regarding an investigation to the public, it may share any information you provide with other law
enforcement agencies, including the Department of Justice.1 While the matter remains open, it
will remain confidential as set forth above. After the matter is closed, certain documents from
the file will be made available to the public on the Commission’s website. To learn more about
the agency’s disclosure policy, please see 81 Fed. Reg. 51, 702 (Aug. 2, 2016),
https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/notice2016-06.pdf.
If you intend to be represented by counsel in this matter, please advise the Commission
by completing the enclosed form stating the name, address and telephone number of such
counsel, and authorizing such counsel to receive any notifications and other communications
from the Commission. Please note that you have a legal obligation to preserve all documents,
records, and materials relating to the subject matter of the complaint until such time as you are
notified that the Commission has closed its file in this matter. See 18 U.S.C. § 1519.
1 The Commission has the statutory authority to refer knowing and willful violations of the Act to the
Department of Justice for potential criminal prosecution, 52 U.S.C. § 30109(a)(5)(C), and to report information
regarding violations of law not within its jurisdiction to appropriate law enforcement authorities. Id. § 30107(a)(9).

Introduction
OlffCE OF GENERAL COUNSB..
Hello:
I am filing this complaint on behalf of my client David Prutzman. David Prutzman owns a small
business (Dave's Campaign and Business Solutions) that produces political yard signs and
performs other types of printing for political campaigns.
Factual Background
In 2022, Loren Culp ran for Congress in Washington State's 41t1 Congressional District.
During this campaign, Culp's committee ordered printed materials from Dave's Campaign and
Business Solutions, a small business owned by David Prutzman.
After losing the election, Culp's campaign committee owed Dave's Campaign and Business
Solutions $4,854.45 for goods that had been provided to the Culp campaign. When Mr. Prutzman
spoke with a member of Culp's campaign team about this debt, they did not dispute the validity of
the debt. The member of Culp's campaign team said only thatthere were no campaign funds with
which to pay the debts owed to Dave's Campaign and Business Solutions.
Mr. Prutzman has made numerous efforts to communicate with Culp's campaign to collect this
debt. These efforts have proven unsuccessful. Mr. Prutzman did not forgive this debt.
The four invoices billed to the Culp campaign which remain unpaid are attached to this complaint.
The invoice numbers are #1677, #174 9, #1781, and #1873.
Violation of FEC Requirements
The FEC website, summarizing legal requirements, notes that: "Unpaid bills and written contracts
or agreements to make expenditures are considered debts. Debts and obligations must be reported
continuously until repaid.,., See 11 CFR 100.112, 11 CFR 104.3(d), 11 CFR 104.11, & 11 CFR Part
116.
Despite this requirement, the Culp campaign failed to disclose the debt on its terminal FEC Form 3
report filed on 11/23/2022.2 This debt was still outstanding at the time this report was filed, and for
all periods covered by the report. No other report filed by the Culp 2022 campaign lists any debt
owed by the campaign.
These debt were originally incurred on 8/31 /21, 11/29/21, 3/10/22, & 4/13/22. See attached
invoices: #1677, #1749, #1781, and #1873.
The Culp campaign has failed to file any FEC Form 3 reports since filing its terminal FEC Form 3
report on 11/23/2022.

FEDERAL ELECTION COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, D.C.

VIA ELECTRONIC MAIL
liz@lizcurtisassociates.com
Elizabeth Curtis, Treasurer
Culp for Congress
P.O. Box 726
Moses Lake, WA 98837
RE: MUR 8350
Culp for Congress
Dear Ms. Curtis:
On November 21, 2024, the Federal Election Commission notified Culp for Congress
(the “Committee,”), and you in your official capacity as treasurer, of a complaint alleging
violations of certain sections of the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as amended (the
“Act”). A copy of the complaint was forwarded to the Committee at that time.
Upon further review of the allegations contained in the complaint, and information
supplied in response, the Commission, on March 12, 2025, voted to dismiss this matter and close
the file effective April 14, 2025. The General Counsel’s Report, which more fully explains the
Commission’s decision, is enclosed for your information.
Documents related to the case will be placed on the public record today. See Disclosure
of Certain Documents in Enforcement and Other Matters, 81 Fed. Reg. 50,702 (Aug. 2, 2016).
Sincerely,
Lisa J. Stevenson
Acting General Counsel
BY: Wanda D. Brown
Assistant General Counsel

RE: MUR 8350
Culp for Congress
Dear Mr. Prutzman:
This is in reference to the complaint filed with the Federal Election Commission on
November 20, 2024, concerning Culp for Congress. Based on that complaint, and after
considering the circumstances of this matter and information provided in response to the
complaint, the Commission determined to dismiss this matter and close the file effective
April 14, 2025.
The General Counsel’s Report, which more fully explains the basis for the Commission’s
decision, is enclosed. Documents related to the case will be placed on the public record today.
See Disclosure of Certain Documents in Enforcement and Other Matters, 81 Fed. Reg. 50,702
(Aug. 2, 2016).
The Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971, as amended, allows a complainant to seek
judicial review of the Commission’s dismissal of this action within 60 days of the dismissal,
which became effective today. See 52 U.S.C. § 30109(a)(8).
Sincerely,
Lisa J. Stevenson
Acting General Counsel

CERTIFICATION
I, Laura E. Sinram, Secretary and Clerk of the Federal Election
Commission, do hereby certify that on March 12, 2025, the Commission
decided by a vote of 4-0 to take the following actions in MUR 8350:
1. Dismiss the Complaint, consistent with the Commission’s prosecutorial
discretion to determine the proper ordering of its priorities and use of
agency resources. Heckler v. Chaney, 470 U.S. 821, 831-32 (1985), as
recommended in the EPS Dismissal Report dated February 28, 2025.
2. Close the file effective 30 days from the date the certification of this
vote is signed (or on the next business day after the 30th day, if the 30th
day falls on a weekend or holiday).
3. Send the appropriate letters.
Commissioners Broussard, Dickerson, Lindenbaum, and Trainor voted
affirmatively for the decision.
